reference.ab:
For three centuries, physics has been divided by a fundamental conceptual chasm.

On one side stands Newtonian mechanics, governing the macroscopic realm through deterministic continuous functions; on the other, quantum mechanics describes the microscopic world via probabilistic wavefunctions and discrete observables.

We demonstrate that this division is an artifact of incomplete mathematical description.

Both frameworks emerge as complementary limiting cases of a deeper, number-theoretic reality: a prime-resonant field where energy, motion, and causality arise directly from the arithmetic structure of prime numbers themselves.

By treating primes as irreducible vibrational modes of the universe’s information substrate, we construct Prime Field Equations that reduce to Newton’s laws in the coherent classical limit and to the Schrödinger equation in the incoherent quantum limit.

The unification is not merely philosophical but provides specific, testable predictions including prime-modulated decoherence spectra, classical motion corrections at atomic precision, and a first-principles derivation of the fine-structure constant α from Riemann zeta zeros.

The framework dissolves the measurement problem, explains the quantum-classical transition, and reveals that determinism and randomness are complementary aspects of prime-phase alignment in a fundamentally arithmetic universe.
